This letter is the Attorney General's order on your petition for disclosure of records
under the Oregon Public Records Law, ORS 192.410 to 192.505. Your petition, which we
received on December 20, 1993, asks the Attorney General to direct the Oregon State
Lottery to make available copies of records that would identify:
How much total revenue each business in Crook, Deschutes and
Jefferson counties that has video poker has earned from each machine
since installation, and how much each business has earned in commissions
from each machine.
The lottery's refusal to disclose the foregoing information was based on
ORS 192.501(5). That subsection of the Public Records Law exempts from disclosure sales
records and similar business records of private businesses which are required by law to be
submitted to a public body, and which are used by the public body to establish quotas. That
provision states in part:
The following public records are exempt from disclosure under
ORS 192.410 to 192.505 unless the public interest requires disclosure
in the particular instance:
* * * * *

(5) Information consisting of production records, sale or purchase
records or catch records, or similar business records of a private concern or
enterprise, required by law to be submitted to or inspected by a governmental
body to allow it to determine fees or assessments payable or to establish
production quotas * * * to the extent that such information is in a form which
would permit identification of the individual concern or enterprise.
The records you request are business records that are required by law - the
administrative rules of the lottery - to be submitted to the lottery. See OAR 177-100-065(1)
(requiring video lottery retail contractors to submit fmancial and operating records to the
lottery). However, after consulting with officials of the lottery, this office and the lottery
have determined that the sales and commission records that relate to video lottery activity are
not used to establish the production quotas that the lottery has established for certain lottery
retail contractors. See OAR 177-40-040(2) (establishing weekly sales quotas for certain
lottery games).
Therefore, the lottery has agreed to permit the inspection of the records identified in
your request. You may contact Marlene Meissner, Public Affairs Assistant for the Lottery,
at 378-3545, to arrange to inspect or obtain copies of the records. The lottery remains
authorized, by ORS 192.440(3), to charge you a fee to reimburse it for its reasonable
expenses in making those records available.
Because the lottery has agreed to make the records available to you, we respectfully
deny your petition as moot.
